selected_evidence.requirement: Record every sudo command with user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log
selected_evidence.summary: Shows the valid native sudo logfile policy, secure file permissions, and timestamped COMMAND entries identifying invoking user antrieb and target user root before and after restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: Keep sudo command entries out of general system logs
selected_evidence.summary: Unique sudo probes were present in the dedicated logfile while matching zero entries in messages, secure, and the journal.

selected_evidence.requirement: Keep the installed legacy operating-system release and kernel
selected_evidence.summary: Both baseline and final checks show RHEL Server 7.9 and kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64.

selected_evidence.requirement: Mandatory node1 restart and recovery evidence
selected_evidence.summary: Healthy baseline boot ID 16724682-15d4-4e48-bfb9-a2913f22f416; acknowledged native delayed reboot; observed shutdown; recovered with changed boot ID 820f2a46-8f6b-4b22-af35-695c248e85ea; system running with rsyslog active/enabled, valid persisted policy, retained pre-restart record, and successful post-restart logging isolation.

commands.command:
set -eu
umask 077
printf '%s\n' 'Defaults logfile="/var/log/sudo-commands.log"' 'Defaults !syslog' > /tmp/99-sudo-command-logging
sudo visudo -cf /tmp/99-sudo-command-logging
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0600 /dev/null /var/log/sudo-commands.log
sudo install -o root -g root -m 0440 /tmp/99-sudo-command-logging /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-command-logging
sudo visudo -c
sudo ls -lZ /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-command-logging /var/log/sudo-commands.log
sudo sed -n '1,20p' /etc/sudoers.d/99-sudo-command-logging
